q: How much power does the Hooghly cold storage cluster use?
title: Hooghly cold stores: power per tonne
short: About 110.9 million kWh and 0.5 million litres of diesel a year across some 150 potato cold stores, 10,073 toe in 2022-23, or roughly 76,000 t CO2. Bigger stores use less per tonne held: about 89 kWh per tonne of capacity below 10,000 t, 46 kWh above 20,000 t.
audience: Potato cold store owners in Hooghly district

ul: 62 stores below 10,000 t (average 6,237 t), 70 at 10,000 to 20,000 t (average 13,704 t), 18 above 20,000 t (average 23,522 t).
Table potatoes are held at 2 to 4 C for up to 6 to 8 months; potatoes for processing at 10 to 12 C.
Chambers rise 4 to 5 floors, 50 to 60 feet.
DG sets, and in some stores diesel engines on the compressors, cover power cuts.
Most systems are reciprocating ammonia compressors, run flat out with manual control, on rewound standard motors.
Ammonia has no global warming potential, so top-ups add nothing; the footprint is power and diesel.
Re-pipe stores built before 2005 if the pressure drop from evaporator to condenser is over 0.2 bar: each 0.1 bar costs about 7% more power.
Re-insulate pipes and valves that frost: 5 to 8% less power, payback within a year.
Controls and VFDs on evaporator fans: about Rs 10 to 12 lakh for a 5,000 t store, payback 18 to 24 months.
Strip or air curtains on chamber doors; none of the surveyed stores had them.

example.title: CO2 per tonne of capacity, by size (estimate)
lines: Above 20,000 t: 738 t + 8 t = 746 t / 23,522 t = 32 kg per tonne
Cluster: 110.9 million kWh = 74,860 t; 0.5 million L diesel = 1,320 t; about 76,200 t
example.note: Power, diesel and capacity from TERI's 2022-23 energy profile of the cluster; per tonne of rated capacity, not tonnes actually stored.

senseible: Enter a season's kWh and diesel in the calculators for CO2 per tonne stored; Senseible can read the WBSEDCL bills and diesel slips into monthly records.
